views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current posture and continue negotiating the Phase One deal without making new unilateral concessions, while preserving our core demand that the US roll back tariffs as part of any settlement. We should engage constructively to keep the deal alive and avoid forcing the US's pending Dec 15 tariffs (List 4B) onto nearly all remaining Chinese exports, using our existing goodwill signals (waived soy/pork duties, exemption lists) as our leverage rather than escalating. Do not concede on tariff rollback or accept a one-sided purchases-only deal.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is real but not existential. China's November exports fell 1.1% YoY for the fourth straight month, with exports to the US down 23% and 12 straight monthly declines (Reuters/BBC, Dec 8), while GDP growth cooled to 6% in Q3, near 30-year lows (AP). Firm-level targeting persists: Huawei remains on the US Entity List since May 16, and Google/Android access was suspended (timeline May 16/20), directly threatening our tech-goals. That justifies a positive threat score near the +0.5 'major export sectors hit / firm-level targeting' anchor. However, it is not existential: the economy has been 'unexpectedly resilient,' imports rose for the first time since April on stimulus (Reuters Dec 8), and we hold asymmetric leverage (rare-earth signal, May 20; unreliable-entity list, May 31) plus diversification (EU exports +4.5%, ASEAN +11.5%). The trajectory is toward de-escalation: a Phase One deal was announced in principle Oct 11, and by Dec 10 reports indicate both sides are 'laying the groundwork' to delay the Dec 15 tariffs (CNBC/WSJ). Escalating now would be self-defeating — it would invite the Dec 15 tariffs onto virtually all remaining exports and deepen the export pain that is already our main vulnerability. Negotiating (action_score +0.2) captures that: engage to secure a deal and avoid new tariffs, hold firm on tariff rollback, and let the opponent's own need to avoid pre-Christmas tariffs work in our favor.
key_factors: China exports fell 4 straight months; US-bound exports down 23% YoY, 12 straight monthly declines
Huawei still on US Entity List; Google/Android suspended — tech-threat to CCP self-sufficiency goals
GDP growth cooled to 6% in Q3, near 30-year lows; imports recovering on stimulus (first rise since April)

China holds leverage: rare-earth signal, unreliable-entity list, diversification to EU/ASEAN
